item.title: Zcash developers propose cutting block interval to 20 seconds just days after NU
item.description:
Zcash developers propose cutting block interval to 20 seconds just days after NU7 upgrade – Link

Zcash developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft ZIP to reduce the target block interval from 25 to 20 seconds for the upcoming NU7.1 upgrade. The recent NU7 upgrade had already cut block times from 75 to 25 seconds.

Faster confirmations could improve ZEC's usability for payments and exchange settlement, even though price action has not yet reflected the protocol news.

item.title: AcryptoS DeFi protocol hacked for ≈$665,000, shuts down operations – Link The De
item.description:
AcryptoS DeFi protocol hacked for ≈$665,000, shuts down operations – Link

The DeFi yield aggregator ACryptoS disclosed a treasury exploit caused by a lack of input validation. Attackers were able to mint a majority of shares in 77 treasuries across 5 chains with minimal deposits. The team disabled deposits, kept withdrawals open, offered a 10% bounty, and said the project is ceasing operations.

Even established-looking DeFi protocols can still carry ongoing smart-contract risk.

item.title: THORChain and Wasabi wallet processed stolen Binance hack funds despite FBI appe
item.description:
THORChain and Wasabi wallet processed stolen Binance hack funds despite FBI appeal – Link

The Wall Street Journal reported that after the recent Binance-linked theft, hackers laundered funds across 10,000+ wallets. THORChain reportedly processed over $46M of stolen funds within 72 hours and collected over $200K in fees, while nearly $4M moved through Wasabi Wallet despite law-enforcement requests to stop processing.

This adds compliance and reputational risk for decentralized infrastructure used in illicit fund flows.

item.description:
Binance hack fallout widens as Fed and OCC begin checking US banks for spillover risk – Link

Following last week's $6.3B Binance security breach, the Federal Reserve and OCC started contacting banks to check for unusual activity or vulnerabilities that could be exploited by similar attack methods.

Regulators appear to be treating the hack as a systemic-risk issue, which could raise scrutiny on exchange security and crypto-bank linkages.

item.title: Chainalysis says Binance hack funds are being laundered through Chinese networks
item.description:
Chainalysis says Binance hack funds are being laundered through Chinese networks – Link

Chainalysis reported that hackers behind the $6.3B Binance theft are routing part of the stolen funds through Chinese money-laundering networks. Earlier reports said Tether and Circle had frozen roughly $823M in stolen USDT/USDC within an hour of the exploit.

The recovery effort is becoming more complex and multi-jurisdictional, keeping pressure on exchange security and stablecoin freeze protocols.

item.title: AI-stock meltdown drags crypto into a $1B+ liquidation cascade – Link The Nasdaq
item.description:
AI-stock meltdown drags crypto into a $1B+ liquidation cascade – Link

The Nasdaq 100 had its worst session since 2020, with AI/chip stocks sliding hard — Nvidia ~-9%, Micron ~-17% — while crypto-linked equities like MSTR, COIN, and CRCL fell 9–13%. Bitcoin dropped over 5% to near $75,600–$76,000, and total crypto liquidations hit about $1.08B, including ≈$954M in longs.

Crypto is still trading like a risk asset tied to tech/AI sentiment, so continued equity volatility could add more downside pressure.

item.title: Zcash activates NU7 upgrade, freezing ≈$16M in oldest privacy pool – Link Zcash'
item.description:
Zcash activates NU7 upgrade, freezing ≈$16M in oldest privacy pool – Link

Zcash's NU7 network upgrade went live, invalidating version-4 transactions and making roughly 12,224 ZEC (≈$15-16M) in the legacy "Sprout" privacy pool unspendable. It also cut block times to roughly a third of previous levels.

The upgrade is a major technical migration for a top-20 privacy coin and may affect throughput, fee dynamics, and legacy fund access.

item.title: Democrats win full control of Congress, raising crypto regulatory uncertainty –
item.description:
Democrats win full control of Congress, raising crypto regulatory uncertainty – Link

Democrats retook both the House and Senate in the US midterms. Crypto-friendly Republicans Bryan Steil, Zach Nunn, and Ann Wagner lost seats, while Sherrod Brown is back in the Senate and Elizabeth Warren and Maxine Waters are positioned for key committee roles.

This lowers the odds of the market-structure/CLARITY Act passing in an industry-friendly form and may point to tighter scrutiny on stablecoins and digital-asset policy.

item.title: North Korean hackers continue laundering $6.3B Binance hack proceeds via THORCha
item.description:
North Korean hackers continue laundering $6.3B Binance hack proceeds via THORChain – Link

The FBI formally attributed the Oct 29 Binance hack to the TraderTraitor group, which has routed stolen SOL and ETH into BTC largely through THORChain swaps. Arkham data says about 81% of stolen SOL moved via the protocol, while Binance says it has restored ≈98% of affected user funds using company reserves.

DeFi cross-chain infrastructure is still hard to police even after attribution, and could increase pressure for address-blocking on THORChain-like protocols.

item.title: DTCС's tokenization service goes live with Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citi, BofA
item.description:
DTCС's tokenization service goes live with Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citi, BofA among first users – Link

Morgan Stanley confirmed it is using DTCC's newly launched DTS platform, live since Oct 28, to tokenize US stocks, ETFs, and Treasuries on-chain. The rollout includes about 20 institutions and runs on the Canton Network and DTCC's private Besu network.

• Coverage includes Russell 1000 constituents and major ETFs.
• Other users include JPMorgan, Citigroup, Bank of America, Fidelity, and Citadel Securities.

The institutional tokenization infrastructure is moving from pilot to real use and could support longer-term on-chain settlement adoption.

item.title: Binance attack traced to fake job interviews and a compromised AI coding tool –
item.description:
Binance attack traced to fake job interviews and a compromised AI coding tool – Link

Binance's investigation found attackers planted a tampered Homebrew package via a fake AI programming tool in June, then used a fake recruiter/interview scheme in September to compromise a second engineer's device. The exploit ultimately used Ethereum's EIP-7702 authorization mechanism to gain partial hot-wallet control.

It shows a multi-month social-engineering plus AI-tooling attack vector that exchanges and custodians may need to audit against.

Aave Labs, Veda Tech Labs, and Kamino Foundation submitted a legal analysis to the SEC arguing that DAO-governed lending vaults should not be classified as securities based solely on manager discretion.

The regulatory outcome could shape whether major DeFi vault products face securities registration requirements.

item.description:
THORChain drops on regulatory and security risk concerns tied to Binance hack laundering – Link

RUNE fell roughly 20% and briefly dipped below $0.50 after on-chain data showed North Korean hackers laundered about $42.7M in stolen Binance funds through THORChain's cross-chain swaps. US agencies have requested node operators block related flows, but co-founders have resisted address-freezing.

It highlights the tension between DeFi censorship resistance and regulatory pressure, which could affect RUNE's risk premium and liquidity.

item.title: Binance raises market maker rebates to defend liquidity after record hack – Link
item.description:
Binance raises market maker rebates to defend liquidity after record hack – Link

Bloomberg says Binance is offering temporary higher rebates to Tier 2/3 market makers, matching Tier 4 rates for one week after Bitcoin order book depth on the exchange fell about 30% within a 1% price range.

It is a direct attempt to stop liquidity flight and spread widening, and its effectiveness will show whether Binance can hold market share.

item.title: XRP Ledger token permission amendment set to activate Wednesday – Link A propose
item.description:
XRP Ledger token permission amendment set to activate Wednesday – Link

A proposed XRPL amendment enabling token-level permissioning has support from 33 of 35 trusted validators and is expected to activate this week. A related proposal to restrict unauthorized token holders remains under separate review.

This could change how issuers manage compliance and access controls on XRPL, especially for institutional and RWA use cases.
